title: "I found it cheaper online"
subtitle: Nine times in ten that is a different fare code, not a better price.

text: A cheaper number is usually a smaller booking.
sub: Same ship, same week, same cabin letter - and a different fare code underneath it, with different inclusions and different terms.

title: Three things the cheaper number quietly dropped

items.head: The bundled inclusions
items.body: Bundled fares and stripped fares look identical on a results page. They are not the same product.

items.head: Refundability
items.body: Non-refundable deposits price lower for a reason. You are being paid a small amount to accept a real risk.

items.head: The cabin you assumed
items.body: Guarantee bookings, obstructed views and connecting doors all sit inside the same category letter.

text: Send me the cheaper one. I'll tell you what it left out.
sub: Occasionally it is genuinely the better buy and I'll say so. More often the two fares are not comparable, and that is the whole finding.

quote: Any search engine can surface a hundred sailings; the work is knowing which three deserve your attention, and why.

title: Screenshot it and send it over
body: I'll read the fare code and the inclusions against it, then come back with a two-line verdict on whether it is actually cheaper.
